evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.text: The study reports numeral 三 in Shang oracle-bone corpus examples H.16189 and H.37453, and says its survey found 三 as the sole graph slot for that numeral in Shang sources. It does not provide a precise date for either inscription or independently reproduce their facsimiles.
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.field: §2.1.2–2.2 周朝、秦汉时期数词用字
evidence.text: The study reports 參 as an additional spelling of the numeral in Zhou sources, including a Western Zhou late-period bronze example; 三 remains dominant. It also reports 品/晶 as a Warring States alternative in Chu manuscript evidence. In excavated Qin-Han sources 三 and 參 occur. These are alternative graphs for the numeral, not evidence that the basic graph 三 was borrowed from another word.
evidence.kind: scholarly article reporting historical orthographic uses
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.field: §2.2 秦汉时期; transmitted Hanshu example
evidence.text: The author excludes a transmitted Hanshu example of 叄 for numeral 三 from the Qin-Han count, proposing it may reflect later character substitution; the survey found no such numeral use in excavated Qin-Han documents. This is a qualified textual-transmission hypothesis, not proof the form could not have been used then.
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Academia Sinica Institute of History and Philology, Xiaoxuetang
evidence.field: 字形演變; 金文 record 集成04261; explanation
evidence.text: The entry lists a bronze-script record identified as 集成04261, Chu manuscript forms and a Small Seal form. It explains the three equal horizontal strokes as three counting rods used to record the number three. The page does not textually describe each early glyph image, and this explanation does not by itself establish that the earliest graph was directly devised by copying physical rods.
evidence.title: 漢字「三」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 三 entry; 許慎 account and 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen account defines 三 as “the way of Heaven, Earth, and humanity” and says it is formed “from the number three”; it also records 弎 as an ancient form written with 弋. Duan Yucai distinguishes the definition from the graphic explanation and comments that the three strokes embody the three powers. This is a later lexicographic account, not an independent Shang attestation. No semantic extension chronology follows from this gloss.
evidence.title: 說文解字「三」

evidence.source: Unicode Consortium mailing-list archive; Mark Davis message
evidence.text: A 2002 Unicode mailing-list message explicitly gives U+4E09 kMandarin SAN1, glossing it 三; sān. This corroborates the current reading in the supplied local Unihan row, but it is not evidence for ancient sound development.
evidence.title: Pinyin Readings (was Re: CJK fonts)

gaps: No original oracle-bone or bronze facsimile was independently inspected. The Shang numeral examples and their corpus classification are reported by a scholarly survey; it gives no precise year or reign for H.16189 or H.37453.

The Xiaoxuetang character-specific query and official rights notice could not be opened, and exact Commons file description pages for both local leads were inaccessible. No direct image URL with independently verified identity and reuse terms could be proposed. The absence of an image here reflects access/provenance limits, not lack of historical glyph candidates.

The counting-rod explanation is the Academia Sinica entry's account; direct descent from physical rods is not independently established. Shuowen's Heaven-Earth-humanity explanation is a historical lexicographic interpretation and should not be conflated with it.

The inspected evidence documents the early numeral function and later alternative spellings, but not a full dated chronology of semantic extensions in the spoken numeral word. No older secondary senses or chronology are inferred from glossary lists.

No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed for 三. Baxter–Sagart's possible influence from 四 concerns the spoken reconstruction and does not establish graphic formation. This pass did not independently verify the comparative Proto-Sino-Tibetan proposal in the dossier.

The supplied local Unihan row is sān; its official character-specific lookup could not be inspected. The supplied Baxter–Sagart rows preserve MC sam / samH and OC *s.rum / *s.r[u]m-s notation; no external primary table page was checked.
No repeated-source bulk extract is recommended: reuse permission and editorial value for a versioned extract were not established.

limitations.text: No glyph image is proposed because the exact Commons description pages for the candidate files could not be fetched, and the Xiaoxuetang 三 query plus its official rights notice were inaccessible. This leaves identity, direct image URL, and reuse terms unverified for this entry.
